source.name: Codex-authored repeated-explanation development
source.notes: Codex synthetic writing, repaired and independently reviewed against definitions frozen at eb8390ac before detector evaluation. The source commit identifies those definitions. Final reviewer context, requested model, reviewed counts, and selection are recorded in runners/results/repeated-explanation-development-review.json; the complete writing is versioned in this dataset pair. Selected 100 hits and 100 no-hits; the complete reviewed pool and surplus remain at Git commit 1f29be1fef04421cdebc6cbb89a2662ff07bf511.

snippets: The invoice email worker stopped reading its queue when a large attachment exceeded its memory allowance. Restarting the worker retried the same invoice at the front of the queue, exhausted memory again, and prevented later invoices from being processed.
The large attachment repeatedly exhausted the worker's memory because every restart returned to that same first invoice, leaving subsequent invoices waiting behind it.
The invoice lists its original total, the credit applied, and the remaining amount to pay. A credit larger than the invoice leaves a balance available for a later invoice.
When a credit is used, the original invoice total remains visible alongside the amount deducted and the amount still due; any unused credit remains available for a subsequent invoice.
Use the wired connection for the presentation laptop. The wireless signal is weak at the lectern, while the tested cable gives the laptop a stable connection there.
The wired option is preferable at the lectern because its tested connection avoids the weak wireless signal.
For this presentation, the cable remains the better connection.
We agreed to keep the paper order pad because the cafe's tablet lost its connection on the terrace, leaving staff unable to send those orders to the kitchen.
Keeping the paper pad was the sensible choice while the terrace connection prevented the tablet from passing orders to the kitchen.
The shop had installed a return tray beside the till to keep customer returns apart from books waiting to be sold. Staff had twice shelved a returned book before its refund was recorded.
The tray separated returned books from sale stock so staff would not put them on a shelf before entering the refund.

The backup destination ran out of space because expired backup folders had not been deleted. The retention task used an old folder prefix, so it stopped recognizing new backups after the naming change. Each night's new folder therefore occupied space without older folders being removed.
The storage filled because the naming change left the retention task looking for an obsolete prefix; old backup folders stayed in place while fresh ones accumulated each night.

Saved views now retain their selected sort order. If you arrange a task list by due date and save the view, it will reopen in that order instead of returning to alphabetical sorting. Each saved view keeps its own choice.

When you return to a saved view, the tasks follow the sorting choice you saved there. A due-date view will stay in due-date order, and another view can keep a different order; opening either one no longer resets it to an alphabetical list.

I recommend Harbour Archive for the finance boxes. It retrieves individual files, whereas Pine Store retrieves whole boxes only. Our requests are usually for one invoice folder, so Harbour avoids bringing an entire box back to the office for a single file.
For normal invoice queries, Harbour's file-level service is preferable because it can return the requested folder without sending the whole box to our office.

An unusually low result can combine a student's usual performance with a bad day. On the next test, that temporary disadvantage may be absent, so the result can rise even if the student's underlying proficiency has not changed.
A later improvement can reflect the disappearance of the temporary factors that helped produce the low initial score, rather than any increase in underlying proficiency.
The initial result may have been depressed by an unusually bad day, and the following result can improve simply because that temporary influence is gone.
Bookings are limited to ninety minutes. The limit leaves part of each afternoon available for other residents instead of allowing one gathering to occupy the shared space for the whole day.

Restricting each gathering to ninety minutes means that the courtyard remains available to more than one household during the afternoon. A single booking should not take up the shared area for the whole day, leaving other residents without an opportunity to use it.

An optical zoom changes the image formed by the lens, while a digital zoom enlarges a smaller part of the image the camera has captured. Enlarging that cropped area can make individual detail look softer.

The digital part of the range takes a portion of the captured picture and expands it. Optical zoom instead changes the picture projected through the lens, so cropping and enlargement account for the softer detail associated with digital zoom.
The address on your parcel cannot be changed now because it has already entered the carrier's network. Please use the carrier's delivery manager to request collection from a local depot instead.
For the first parcel, depot collection through the carrier remains the recommended route: the parcel is already in their network, so we can no longer amend its delivery address.

Let's keep Thursday's call at half past ten. Moving it would require the interpreter to cancel another booking, and all three participants have already confirmed this slot. The existing time is the workable choice.
On timing, we should stay with half past ten on Thursday.

Please ask the translator for an editable document rather than a PDF. We still need to insert the final product codes, and an editable file lets the production team do that without rebuilding the page.
For delivery, the editable document remains the right choice because production can add the final codes without reconstructing the layout.

The trial should continue with the current booking sheet. It lets the caretaker resolve overlapping requests before residents send invitations, and all three overlaps this month were settled that way. Replacing it with an open online calendar would remove that confirmation step unless we also built an approval process.
Keeping the present booking sheet is the better course because its confirmation step catches overlapping requests before invitations go out.

Staff can record the time a participant joins without changing the session's scheduled start. The attendance export carries both times, so organizers can distinguish an on-time session from an individual arriving after it began.
Late-arrival records preserve the planned session time and separately store when the participant joined, allowing the export to distinguish session timing from individual punctuality.

A pinned note stays above the chronological note list until unpinned, making access arrangements or equipment changes easier to find. Several notes can be pinned, and their order follows the time each was pinned.
Pinned notes remain at the head of the note list until staff unpin them, with multiple pinned notes arranged by their pinning times.
Photos arrive before the album index, so the pictures can be visible while their albums remain empty.
The empty albums are a result of the index arriving after the photos; the images have reached the phone before their album membership has been applied.

An item can now have several supplier codes attached to one stock record. Scanning any of those codes opens the same item and changes the same stock balance, so receiving a substitute carton does not create another item.
The new code mapping means that different suppliers' barcodes point to one item and one stock balance instead of making separate records for substitute packaging.
Alternative codes share the existing item's stock record, with every recognized supplier code updating that single balance.

Students who already read regularly may be more willing to record their reading. If they are more likely to return a diary, the average calculated from returned diaries will overstate reading time across the invited group.

The estimate from the diaries can be too high because regular readers may be more inclined to take part and send their records back. Their greater representation among respondents would make the returned diaries describe more reading than occurs, on average, among all the students who were invited.

The foyer player had lost its network connection before downloading Wednesday's schedule. It continued showing its last complete schedule, which was Tuesday's, rather than displaying a blank screen. The schedule editor had published the new title correctly to the server.
The old concert title remained on screen because the disconnected foyer player kept its last downloaded schedule; Wednesday's correctly published schedule had not reached it.

Anonymous links now discard the visitor's email address before a response is saved. The resulting response has no email field that an owner can export, even if the visitor arrived from an email campaign.
Anonymous responses contain no exportable email address because the visitor's address is removed before storage, including when the visitor comes through a campaign email.
The caterer orders ingredients from that count on Thursday morning, so names added afterwards may leave us short of meals. We need the final number before that order goes through.
The Wednesday count matters because it becomes the caterer's ingredient order the following morning. Late additions can leave fewer meals than guests, which is why we need the total settled first.

It can clean after the last rehearsal at 22:30, while Bay Services offered an early-morning slot only. Late cleaning suits our schedule because the first group enters before reception opens and needs the rooms ready on arrival.
Fern's evening slot remains the better arrangement: cleaning after the final rehearsal leaves the rooms ready for the early group, unlike Bay's morning-only offer.
Write the variety and sowing date on a label in each tray. Seedlings can look alike before their true leaves develop, so the label preserves an identification you may be unable to recover by sight.
Record germination against the sowing date rather than the day you first notice growth. That gives each batch the same starting point when comparing how long emergence took.
The tray label keeps the variety identifiable while young plants are still too similar to tell apart.
Counting from sowing gives every batch a common starting event, unlike counting from when you happen to notice the shoots.
A consistent guide can see which tasks have already been covered and avoid beginning the introduction again each day. That should leave more of the morning for supervised practice.
Keeping one guide across the three mornings means that person knows what has already been introduced, reducing the time spent restarting the same explanations.

Draft observations are now saved locally as you type. If the app closes before you submit an observation, reopening it restores the unfinished text on that device. Drafts are not shared with the team until submitted.
Unfinished entries return when the app is reopened because their text is saved on the device during editing; they remain private drafts until submission.
Draft text is kept locally during entry, allowing an interrupted, unsubmitted observation to reopen with its previous wording on the same device.
I recommend Vale because it uses the toner cartridges already stocked for the upstairs printer. Moor needs a different cartridge, which would create a second consumables stock for reception.
Vale shares the upstairs machine's cartridge type, allowing reception to use the toner stock we already hold instead of maintaining another type for Moor.
Vale is the choice that keeps us on the existing toner supply rather than adding a second cartridge line.
A replacement carries the remaining time on that warranty rather than starting another two-year period, so the cover ends on 18 February.
The replacement's warranty therefore runs only until 18 February: it takes over the unused portion of your original cover rather than beginning a fresh two years.

Removable describes how the cover attaches to the sofa; the care label describes which cleaning process the fabric and construction can tolerate. A zip therefore tells you that you can take the cover off, rather than that it can go into a washing machine.
The fact that a cover unzips concerns access to the cushion, while its label governs the treatment it can withstand. Being able to remove it is separate from being able to machine-wash it.
We use the production code on the box to match the cut, because pieces from another printing can have the same picture but different shapes.
Matching the box's production code lets us send the correct shape, since a different print run can show the identical image with a different piece cut.
Cans draw from the stored supply slowly enough for neighbouring plots to share it during the dry spell. A hose can empty it before the next refill.
Use watering cans because the slower draw leaves a share of the stored water for other plots; connecting a hose risks draining the tank before it is filled again.
Keep seed heads out of the compost bays as well: seeds can survive in the cooler edges and return to plots when the compost is spread.
Seeds left on discarded flower heads may survive around the bay's cooler edges and germinate after the compost goes onto a bed, which is why those heads belong outside the compost.

Using a room for an exhibition means giving up its best available alternative use during that period. The opportunity cost is the value of that forgone alternative, even when the museum already owns the room.
Ownership does not remove the opportunity cost: occupying the room with the exhibition still sacrifices the value of the best alternative use for those dates.
When a planner in another time zone opens that route, the departure time stays tied to the depot instead of shifting to the planner's local time.
A route continues to show its departure in the depot's time zone even when the person viewing it works elsewhere, rather than converting it to that person's local time.

West Ledger also includes corrections requested within three working days of a pay run; Harbour charges 30 pounds for each corrected run. Our managers often submit late overtime, so included corrections favor West Ledger. West Ledger is the better fit for the way our hours are finalized.
Because late overtime frequently leads to corrections, West Ledger's included correction service suits our pay process better. West Ledger is the better fit for the way our hours are finalized.
We put the children's coats on low hooks so they could collect them without an adult lifting each one down.
The trays under the boots were there to catch mud before it spread onto the classroom floor.
Having the hooks within reach meant the children could take their own coats rather than waiting for an adult to retrieve them.
The boot trays collected the mud so it would not be carried across the classroom floor.

Travel costs should use the project visited, even when the person travelling belongs to another team. That places the expense beside the work that caused it and gives project managers a complete view of their delivery costs.
The cost belongs with the work that prompted the trip, which is why we allocate it to the visited project rather than the traveller's own team. This keeps the project's delivery total complete.
Give each storage box a number and put that number on its contents list. The number connects the list to the physical box even when several boxes look alike.
Numbering the boxes links each inventory to the right container, so identical-looking boxes can still be distinguished.
Keep the numbering system: matching the list number to the box number identifies which of the similar boxes holds the listed items.
Please keep the current camera rather than exchange it. The replacement uses the same mounting plate, so swapping units would leave the loose fixing that lets the picture move.
An exchange is therefore the wrong option here: keep this camera.
The gate reader uses a stored list that updates overnight, so a membership renewed this afternoon will work at the gate tomorrow morning.
For gate access, today's renewal reaches the reader during the overnight update, which is why the card will begin opening the gate tomorrow.
The card's delay is simply the reader waiting for tonight's membership-list refresh; after that refresh your renewed membership will be recognized tomorrow morning.

A loose waste-pipe joint above the room leaked whenever the upstairs sink drained. Water ran along the ceiling void before reaching the visible drip, so the leak appeared several metres from the sink itself.

The separation between the sink and the drip resulted from water following the ceiling void after escaping the loose waste joint. The joint leaked on drainage, carrying water away from the sink before it emerged beside the archive room.
The sink's waste joint allowed drain water into the ceiling void, where it travelled to the drip point rather than falling directly beneath the sink.

The presentation sockets are controlled by a timed contactor intended to switch them off after evening events. Its clock was set twelve hours out, so the programmed 02:00 shutdown occurred at 14:00 instead.
The room's ordinary light switch did not restore the sockets because the timed contactor was still open.
The controller's twelve-hour clock error moved the intended 02:00 socket shutdown to the afternoon, and the open contactor meant the wall light switch could not restore presentation power.
The afternoon interruption happened because a clock twelve hours out applied the overnight contactor shutdown during the day; the ordinary light switch could not override that contactor.

We should choose the Finch machine rather than the Alder. Finch's removable water tank can be filled at the kitchen sink, whereas Alder needs a permanent water connection beside the machine. The foyer has no suitable connection, so Finch fits the room as it stands.
Finch is the appropriate choice because its tank can be taken to the sink, avoiding a permanent water supply that the foyer lacks.

Please put comments on the spring brochure in the shared proof by Thursday afternoon. The designer will work from that file, so comments sent as separate attachments may be missed when the changes are assembled. Keeping the feedback in one proof gives her a single version to update.

All brochure feedback needs to stay in the shared proof so that the designer has one version containing the changes. Separate annotated attachments can leave comments outside the file she is working from, which is why I am asking everyone to comment in the same place.
We moved the rehearsal to the upstairs room because roadworks outside the ground-floor windows made the piano difficult to hear.
The upstairs location avoided the road noise that had been drowning out the piano downstairs.
Holding the session above ground level kept us away from the roadworks that obscured the piano in the lower room.
Use the seated portrait. It has enough clear space above the speaker's head for the programme heading, whereas the standing photograph would force the heading over her face.
The seated image is the choice to make here: it leaves room for the heading without placing words across her face.

Reed Workwear can supply individual sizes from stock, so a replacement can be ordered for one guide. Hill Stitch requires a minimum of ten garments per repeat order. Because new guides join in small numbers, Reed avoids buying a batch when we need one shirt.
Reed's single-garment repeat orders suit small intakes of new guides and prevent us having to purchase ten shirts just to replace one.

The test shirt's stitched emblem remained legible after the sample washes, whereas the transfer's fine lettering began to lift. The stitched version is preferable for shirts that will be washed after every shift.
The pocket emblem is stitched rather than transferred, keeping its lettering readable through the frequent washing required after shifts.

An estimated water bill uses a calculated reading in place of a recent reading from your meter. The supplier compares that estimate with the previous billed reading to work out the volume charged. If the estimate is too high, the bill can include water you have not yet used.

The estimated figure substitutes for a meter observation the supplier has not received. Usage is then calculated by subtracting the earlier billed figure from that substitute, so an overestimate can charge for more water than has passed through the meter.
A request does not change the due date until a desk worker approves it. The borrower sees Pending beside the proposed date, and the existing due date remains visible.
The current due date stays in force while an extension awaits approval; sending the request alone does not move it, and the proposed date is marked Pending.

The garden committee recommends keeping one combined seed order this spring. Buying together reaches the supplier's free-delivery threshold, while separate small orders would each attract postage. The saving can go toward replacement labels and trays.
A single order remains the sensible option because it avoids the postage attached to individual orders and qualifies for free delivery. Labels and trays can be bought with the money saved.
We decided to keep the existing noticeboard because its glass cover protected the walking-group notices from rain.
Keeping the covered noticeboard was the right choice for protecting the notices from rain.
A tag links the bicycle to an owner's reply, so volunteers can distinguish an unclaimed bicycle from one whose owner has confirmed it is still in use.
The numbered tag connects each bicycle with the reply made by its owner, allowing the volunteers to separate confirmed bicycles from those still awaiting a claim.

The frame width is the distance across the front of the glasses, while the arm length measures the side piece that reaches toward the ear. Two frames can have similar lens sizes and still sit differently because their bridges and outer edges differ. Use the full frame measurements rather than the lens width alone.
Overall front width and side-arm length describe different dimensions of fit. Matching only the lens size leaves differences in the bridge and outer frame that can alter where the glasses sit.
Seat charges are based on the members present when the billing month begins. Removing three members on 9 April therefore changes the seat count for May, while the April charge stays at twelve seats.

The three removals happened after the month had started, so they do not reduce this month's bill. We take the seat count at the start of each billing month, which is why April still reflects twelve members and the lower count takes effect in May.
I recommend the minibus for this trip.
The minibus is the option I recommend for this journey.
I favor Hazel because a site measurement puts responsibility for the panel sizes with the supplier rather than the office. Hazel is the safer choice for obtaining panels that fit.

The site measurement in Hazel's offer leaves the supplier responsible for sizing the panels, instead of making office staff supply the final dimensions. Hazel is the safer choice for obtaining panels that fit.
I recommend keeping the original train booking and changing the passenger name. The operator allows a name correction on this fare for 8 pounds, while cancelling would forfeit the fare.
Keeping the booking and correcting the name remains the best route because the 8-pound correction avoids losing the fare through cancellation.

The history service exhausted its database connection pool. A new export path retained its connection while waiting for a file upload to finish. As exports accumulated, ordinary history requests waited for a free connection and reached their timeout before one became available.

History requests timed out because export jobs were occupying the available database connections while their files uploaded. With those connections still held by exports, the history service had to wait, and some requests exceeded the time allowed for a response.
A translation can preserve a word's reference while losing its sound pattern. A pun depending on similar sounds may then cease to work.
The footnote makes the translator's intervention visible instead of presenting the explanation as part of the original dialogue.
When similar sounds carry the joke, changing those sounds can remove the pun even if the translated words keep their ordinary reference.
Putting this explanation below the text shows that it comes from the translator rather than from a speaker in the original scene.

During an automatic defrost cycle, a heater melts frost from the cooling coils. The water travels through a drain into a tray near the compressor, where it gradually evaporates. A short dripping or trickling sound can come from that water moving through the drain.

The occasional trickle has a separate explanation from the hum. Frost is melted off the coils by the defrost heater, then the resulting water drains to the tray by the compressor and evaporates. Hearing that water pass through the drain can be part of the automatic defrost cycle.
Please leave the accession numbers visible on the ends of the archive boxes. Those numbers connect each box to its catalogue entry, so covering them makes it difficult to find a requested item.
Keeping the accession number uncovered preserves the link between the physical box and the catalogue, which is how we locate the material when someone requests it.
We will also keep the empty boxes in the storeroom rather than flatten them; their fitted inserts are needed when the material goes back after photography.
For the return, the fitted packaging needs to remain available, so retain the emptied boxes instead of breaking them down.

A missing name in a surviving passenger list can mean that the person did not travel, but it can also mean that the relevant page was lost. Absence from the surviving document therefore leaves those two possibilities open.
Someone absent from the surviving list may either have stayed behind or appeared on a page that has since disappeared.
Pooling samples from several plots gives one combined measurement. It hides variation between plots because the laboratory receives their contents together.
A very abundant species can dominate that combined result, leaving a rare species with little influence on the average.
Combining the plots removes the separate plot measurements, so differences between locations disappear inside the pooled sample.
The common species will still account for most of the combined average, while the scarce one contributes relatively little.
Locked objects now stay in place while you select or move nearby objects. Locking a display case prevents accidental movement without hiding it from the plan.
Keeping a case locked stops it being shifted inadvertently while surrounding objects are moved, with the case still visible in the drawing.
Download the route map before leaving home. Parts of the valley have no mobile reception, so a map stored on the phone remains available where an online map may not load.
Keep an offline copy of the route, since gaps in valley reception can prevent the phone from loading an online map.
The downloaded map is the better choice here because it stays on the device when mobile reception drops out.
Its handle interrupted the door sensor, so the control system treated the door as obstructed and refused a new call from that landing. The door looked closed from the corridor.
The trolley handle was breaking the landing-door sensor's path, causing the system to read an obstruction and reject ground-floor calls despite the door appearing shut.
Let the brush dry with its bristles pointing down or lying flat. Water left running into the handle can loosen the attachment between the bristles and the handle.
Drying with the bristles downward keeps water from travelling into the handle and weakening the bristle attachment.
The reason for keeping the wet bristles below the handle is to prevent water reaching the joint that holds them in place.
The smaller freezer is sufficient for the annex.
The smaller model has enough capacity for the annex.
For these observations, a straight line is inadequate because the residuals rise at both ends and fall in the middle.
A straight line is therefore inadequate for these observations.
Repairing the existing bridge is the route we should take.
Repairing the existing bridge is the course to choose.
I recommend Willow because one large recycling bin leaves enough space for the caretaker to move the general-waste bin without shifting another bin first.
Willow's single large recycling bin keeps the courtyard route workable, since the caretaker can wheel out general waste without moving a second recycling bin out of the way.

On this scheme, pausing skips deliveries and their charges for the weeks you select. Your account stays open, with the same box size and delivery address ready for the next active week. You do not need to create another subscription when the pause ends.

The pause leaves your membership in place while withholding the chosen boxes and their weekly payments. The saved size and address remain attached to the account, allowing the normal delivery to resume without a new subscription.
For the weeks covered by the pause, there is no box and no charge, but the account remains ready to restart.

Lightly sand the glossy areas until they look dull. The aim is to give the primer a surface it can grip, rather than remove all the old paint. A smooth, glossy coating gives the next coat less purchase, so dulling it helps the new finish stay attached.

The preparation works because reducing the gloss gives the primer something to hold onto. There is no need to take away every layer of sound paint; making the slippery, shiny surface dull improves the grip of the coating that goes over it.
Images that cross the centre need that allowance so the fold does not hide part of the picture; it is included automatically and does not add to the price.
The allowance prevents the centre fold from swallowing part of a photograph spread across two pages, and the automatic addition is already included in the quoted price.
The hall has sixty seats, and advance tickets let the organisers keep admissions within that number rather than turning people away after they arrive.
Advance collection controls the audience against the hall's sixty available seats, avoiding a situation where people arrive only to find there is no place.

Use the recorded interview rather than the recollection written a week later when quoting the participant. The recording preserves the participant's wording; the later account may substitute the researcher's phrasing.
For quotations, the recorded interview remains the right source because it retains the participant's words instead of the researcher's later reconstruction.
The seal and locating tabs need to fit the jug, or water can pass around the cartridge instead of through the filter material.

For the fitting itself, the important point is that the cartridge's tabs and seal match the holder. Otherwise some water takes a route past the filter rather than through it, even though the cartridge is sitting in the jug.
I would choose the specified replacement. The correct model closes the route around the cartridge by matching the seal and tabs, making the water pass through the filtering material.
The carrier reference belongs to that particular crate, so mixing the labels can send a crate against the wrong collection record. We need to keep each reference with its matching crate.
Because the collection reference is specific to the crate, the matching return label needs to stay with that crate rather than enter a shared pile.
Keeping the labels paired with their original crates prevents the wrong collection reference being used for a case.

We are asking for washed, wearable coats rather than bags of unsorted clothing. Volunteers have room to hang coats immediately, but the cupboard has no laundry facilities and little space for sorting other garments. Ready-to-wear coats can reach households sooner.
The collection is restricted to clean coats people can wear straight away because we cannot wash them or sort mixed clothing bags in the space available. That makes them quicker to pass on.

The booking application sent its jobs to a printer name that had been retired during Friday's equipment change. The new printer worked under a different name, but the application's saved printer setting still pointed to the old queue. Jobs remained in that queue without reaching the new machine.
The application was still targeting the retired printer queue, so its jobs could not reach the replacement printer even though normal documents used the new printer name.
We gave each bicycle a numbered tag so the mechanics could take repairs in arrival order without asking everyone when they had joined the queue.
The tags let the mechanics follow arrival order without repeatedly asking people who had come first.
Numbering the bicycles had been intended to preserve the arrival sequence without relying on the owners to reconstruct it.

Objects made from stone are more likely to survive in this soil than objects made from wood. The excavated collection can therefore overrepresent stone tools relative to the tools people actually used.
Because wooden objects decay more readily here, stone objects have a better chance of reaching the excavation; the recovered tools can consequently make stone use appear more common than it was.
The museum gave each borrowed object a temporary number so photographs and condition notes could be matched to the right item before formal accessioning.
Temporary numbers connected the photographs and condition descriptions with their corresponding objects while the formal accession records were still pending.

The captions are available with your recording, but they are stored as a separate file. Your video player reads that file alongside the video, which is why moving only the video to the shared drive removed the captions from playback.
The missing words on screen result from the caption file being separate from the movie; copying the movie alone leaves the player without the accompanying text.
Clay and firing are charged separately according to the work each student makes. This keeps a student making a few small pieces from paying the same materials amount as someone making large pots.
Materials are billed against what an individual makes rather than shared equally across the class. A few small items therefore attract a different materials cost from several large pots.

We need storage for the six sample trays used in a teaching session, plus two trays prepared in advance. Elm holds eight trays in the arrangement we tested. Dene holds twelve. Elm is sufficient for the planned teaching stock.
An eight-tray freezer covers the six session trays and the two prepared beforehand. Elm is sufficient for the planned teaching stock.
For the purchase record, the required load is eight trays and Elm accommodates it. Elm is sufficient for the planned teaching stock.

Until then, paid orders had sat behind the counter among books waiting to be priced. Twice that month, a paid book had been put out for sale. Giving paid orders a separate shelf was meant to stop staff mistaking them for unsold stock.

Keeping the paid books on their own shelf separated them from stock that still needed pricing. The point was to prevent a member of staff from treating a customer's purchase as an unsold book and putting it on the shop floor.
We moved the sign-in table inside because rain had soaked the forms at the previous market.
The yellow badges identified stallholders, allowing the gate volunteer to distinguish them from early shoppers.
Bringing registration under the roof kept the paperwork out of the rain that had damaged it last time.
The yellow badges showed which arrivals had stalls, making them distinguishable from customers arriving before opening.
Both contacts receive renewal notices, but the household still gets one invoice. Adding another contact therefore gives both people the renewal information without creating a second charge.
For renewals, two billing contacts mean both receive the notice while only one invoice is issued to the household. This lets both contacts see the renewal without duplicating the charge.
Sending renewal notices to both billing contacts does not create another household invoice; both receive the information and the household is charged once.

The document generator reused a session object and failed to clear its time field between bookings. When the next booking had no optional arrival note, the generator skipped the field refresh and printed the earlier time. The saved booking record was correct.
The wrong times came from the reused generator object: an absent arrival note caused it to retain the prior booking's time, even though the booking record itself held the requested slot.
A mirror fogs when moist room air meets glass cold enough for some of that moisture to become liquid on its surface. The tiny droplets scatter light, giving the glass its cloudy appearance.
The cloudy coating forms because water vapour in the room turns into small liquid drops on the cooler mirror. Those drops spread the reflected light, which is why the reflection looks misty.
Whatever product you choose, the basic cause is moisture becoming droplets on colder glass. The droplets interrupt the clear reflection.

The downstairs room now closes at four because the evening language classes need its tables. We moved the local-history books upstairs so people consulting them could continue until the building closes at seven.
Moving the local-history collection upstairs means it remains available until seven, after the downstairs room is taken over for classes at four.

The front-page panel was cached separately from the opening-hours page. Updating the page cleared its cache but did not clear the panel's cache, so the panel kept serving its earlier copy. The two displays therefore diverged even though both originated from the same hours record.
Because the home panel had its own cache, clearing the edited hours page left that panel serving the old closing time from the same underlying record.
The one-hour limit prevents one group from taking the whole evening and gives several groups a chance to use the room.
Limiting a booking to an hour leaves room in the evening for more groups instead of allowing a single group to occupy every available slot.
An evening shared between several groups is the reason for the hourly limit: one booking should not consume the whole period.
Try the cleaner on a hidden patch first and let that patch dry. A product can alter the finish even when it removes the dirt, and the dry test shows whether the appearance has changed.
The hidden test matters because removing dirt and preserving the finish are separate results: the dried patch reveals any change caused by the cleaner.

Ask contributors to state how many portions each recipe makes. A serving count allows someone cooking for a different number of people to adjust the ingredient quantities. Keep the contributor's stated yield even when you change the layout or shorten the introduction.

A recipe's serving count tells the reader how many people the stated quantities will feed. That lets a household increase or reduce the ingredients to suit its own table. Preserve that number when preparing the pages; changing the page design or cutting introductory wording should leave the contributor's yield intact.

Place a ruler beside each small object when taking the archive photographs. It gives the person viewing the image a size reference, since the object may look larger or smaller on a screen. Keep the ruler in the same plane as the part being measured to avoid a misleading comparison.

An image on a screen can make a small object look large or a large one look small. Including a ruler supplies a reference against which its dimensions can be judged. Position that reference at the same depth as the surface you are measuring, because a ruler closer to the camera can suggest the wrong relative size.

A temporary download link works until its expiry time. After that time, the same address will no longer open the file, even if it remains in your email. Ask the sender for a new link when that happens; repeatedly opening the expired address will not renew it.

The time limit is what makes the link temporary. Once its expiry has passed, the address in the message stops providing access to the file. Returning to that old address does not reset the deadline. The sender needs to issue another link if you still require access after the first one has expired.

The number on a water meter is a running total, not the amount used since the last bill. The supplier subtracts the earlier reading from the later one to calculate the volume used between those dates.
The meter itself records a cumulative total; the supplier works out consumption by taking the previous reading away from the latest one.

A survey weight describes how much a respondent contributes to an estimate. If younger residents respond less often than older residents, giving each response the same weight can leave younger residents underrepresented. We can increase the contribution of their responses so the age distribution of the weighted sample matches the town's population figures.
Weighting lets a response count more or less towards the result; increasing the contribution from an underrepresented age group brings its weighted share into line with the population.

The full-resolution original stays available for print because the smaller file is a separate copy; the reduced version is easier to attach to an email.
